analysis:
Examined the LaunchAgent.swift patch and the configuration.md head text. The code change adds the literal "DARKBLOOM_TTFT_GDN_BLOCKED" to the LaunchAgent inference passthrough env allow-list (hunk near lines 276-295), plus a doc comment. The docs add the matching row at configuration.md line 414 and bump the date. The variable only selects a Gated DeltaNet prompt-window kernel: `0/false/no/off` keep the stock kernel, `packed`/`rows` force a kernel, and anything else probes. The documented default probe keeps a kernel only where it is bit-exact with `gated_delta_step`. It carries no secrets, authorization, attestation, cache key, or network inputs.

Threat-model checks: A-001 and TB-007/T-041 are unaffected because the variable does not touch prefix-cache keys, TTL, encryption, or scope. TB-003/T-013 and TB-011 are unaffected because the allow-list is the daemon's launch environment, which the local operator already controls. The change only lets an operator's rollback reach the job, as with sibling keys. It is not an attestation or authorization surface, so A-015/A-016 and T-052..T-058 are unaffected. The env scrubber list (DYLD_*, etc.) is unchanged. Residual: a forced `packed` or `rows` kernel skips the parity check and could affect output correctness. That is operator-controlled and documented as for A/B measurement only, so it is outside the adversarial provider model beyond the existing T-007 (a malicious provider can already serve manipulated outputs). The kernel reader in libs/mlx-swift-lm GatedDelta.swift was not supplied, so I did not verify the described semantics. No findings.
